reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker promotes a Bitconnect lending opportunity by reporting investment earnings, asking viewers to sign up through the description link, join his team, and make money together. The video also discusses referrals and loans, displays a referral banner, and separately solicits donations to the speaker's wallet.

letting it build up to about twenty, thirty before every invest
Sign up for bitconnect here https://bitconnect.co/?ref=BundleKing

opening.argument: The speaker presents a personal update rather than a promise of guaranteed results. He reports his own figures, says he is considering letting the balance build, and describes a possible reinvestment choice rather than telling viewers that returns are certain. His wording also distinguishes the reported earnings from affiliate bonuses and attributes them to compounding. That is commentary about one account experience, not a guarantee that every viewer will profit.

citations.quote: I have $9 1 72 cents right now my lending wallet thinking about letting it build up
I think I might do that right now
no affiliate bonuses this is all loan when this is all interest that I grew no from compound compound

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats a referral link and discussion of compounding as proof of deceptive solicitation, but the quoted material does not establish a guaranteed return. The speaker describes what he personally reports and openly says he is still deciding whether to let the balance build. The dashboard likewise identifies the displayed amount as lending profit and shows no affiliate bonus, which is consistent with a personal account update rather than proof of a downline scheme.

citations.quote: thinking about letting it build up
no affiliate bonuses

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A personal tone does not remove the solicitation. The speaker explicitly says viewers can sign up, join his team, and get the money together, while the description supplies a Bitconnect sign-up URL. His statement that compounding makes it possible to make money presents the lending activity as an earning opportunity, not merely neutral commentary. The absence of the word “guaranteed” does not negate that message.

opening.argument: The video can be understood as a hands-on demonstration of an account interface and a first-person progress update. The speaker identifies it as day 20, explains the amount in his lending wallet, and says he intends to document his journey and make another video at a later balance. The sampled screen shows account fields for total investment, lending profit, affiliate bonus, and total earned. That format supports an operational walkthrough or personal review, without independently proving that viewers are being deceived.

citations.quote: this is day 20 just want to give you an update
I am going to document this
I Make another video somewhere around the fifteen dollar mark

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the video a promotion overlooks its demonstrative structure. The speaker walks through his own balance, explains how he is considering compounding, and plans a follow-up at a specified balance. The screen is an account-style display, not a testimonial from unnamed customers or evidence of a promised outcome. A link appearing in the description does not by itself establish that the primary purpose is deceptive solicitation.

citations.quote: I have $9 1 72 cents right now my lending wallet
I Do another video

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The operational demonstration is precisely what makes the promotion persuasive: it displays a $400 investment and $49.39 in lending profit while the speaker explains how to compound and invites viewers to sign up. He does not merely inspect the interface; he says viewers can join his team and that they can get money together. The follow-up framing therefore documents and markets the supposed earning opportunity at the same time.

citations.quote: it is possible to make money without getting referrals all you have to do is compound
if you want to be a part of my team

opening.argument: At most, the evidence shows ordinary referral promotion around a cryptocurrency service and a request for voluntary support. The description says “Sign up” and mentions donating to the speaker's wallet, while the speaker says he has referrals but no earnings from them. The dashboard shows an affiliate bonus of $0.00 alongside lending profit, so the supplied material does not establish downline income, a required deposit from viewers, credential collection, or a guaranteed payout. Those missing mechanisms matter before classifying the content as deceptive.

citations.quote: If you would like to donate to me here is my bitconnect wallet
I think I've got three or four referrals that signed up but nobody is doing loans right now so that's why I haven't made anything off referrals
if you want to be a part of my team

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution infers a scam mechanism from ordinary referral language, but the record says the speaker has made nothing from referrals and the displayed affiliate bonus is $0.00. The donation request is separately described as support, with no promised benefit stated in the supplied material. A sign-up URL and a wallet address show promotion or support channels, but they do not prove a guaranteed return, credential request, or downline payment.

citations.quote: nobody is doing loans right now so that's why I haven't made anything off referrals
if there's anybody that wants to support me
If you would like to donate to me here is my bitconnect wallet

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The relevant mechanism is not limited to affiliate bonuses. The video reports $400 invested and $49.39 in lending profit, then tells viewers they can sign up, join his team, and get money together. It also says compounding makes it possible to make money without referrals. Thus the central pitch is participation in a lending-return program; the $0 affiliate field does not make that investment promotion ordinary commerce.
